message:
Give each branch of a Run its own writer lease and status

claim_branch locks a branch's own worker-lock after taking the Run's gate
for a moment, so writers of different branches work at once. claim_run,
for operations on a whole Run, holds the gate and refuses while any branch
is written. Only exclusive locks are used, as Windows offers. Each branch
records its computation status in its own status.json, version 1; the
Run's status becomes their summary. Recovery interrupts branches left
running without a writer and forgets the status of a fork's child that
was never created.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Compute and fork branches of one Run at once

ProjectAPI keeps a job per branch: a branch computes or is created by one
job at a time, and other branches of the Run, or other Runs, run up to
the limit. A fork waits only for its source branch. Cancelling with a
branch_id stops that branch; without one, the whole Run. Computations,
forks, the CLI and TimelineStore.advance take branch leases and record
branch statuses. Index writers wait up to two minutes for another
branch's write.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Describe branch leases, branch statuses and per-branch cancel

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Show and control each branch's computation on the project screen

The screen read the Run's status, which is running while any branch
computes, so every branch's buttons were disabled and a fork waited for
other branches to stop. It now reads the selected branch's status: its
compute, fork and preview buttons are disabled only while it computes,
the branch list marks computing branches, a fork ends when its child is
listed and still or its outcome failed, and cancel stops the selected
branch. A Run without branch statuses still uses its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

message:
Check a save's restore by comparing it with the world just validated

The restore check of a cached capture builds the world from the saved document
and compares it with the world validated before the capture. An equal world
passes the same validation, so it is not validated again; a different one is.
EventLog records an earlier check found equal are not compared again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Parse only recent shared-operation records before an append

record_shared_operation validated the whole shared operations state, up to
20,000 records, on every append. Like per-tick validation it now parses the
records since the previous tick; the duplicate check reads the same records,
since a record carries its event's realized minute, the current one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read only the checked event types and new records in full validation

The EventLog keeps indexes by event type and by provenance object as records
are appended, and EventsById looks events up through its ID index. The
operational, EffectProgram, environment and infrastructure checks read only the
event types they check, without copying the log into a dict. The EventLog audit
checks only records added since its last audit while the earlier ones are still
the same leading objects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

End a thread job's status, lease and entry together under the API lock

A thread job wrote its final status, recorded telemetry, then released its
lease and left the job table. A client that saw the status and submitted the
next job at once was refused as busy. The three now end together under the
lock a submit takes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Check each social and body relationship record inline every tick

Every tick checks every relationship (about 9,800 at day 7). The record checks
now compare key views with a constant set and read the counts directly instead
of building a set and running generators per record, accepting exactly what
the field-by-field rules accepted.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

message:
Measure the end of a saved Run and compare hashes in the benchmark

investigate_performance.py can fork a saved Run's main branch at a minute and
compute a short window from there, so the last day's saves and ticks are
measured without computing the whole Run again. --expect compares the world,
events and KPI hashes with an earlier result and exits 1 on a mismatch.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Compute psychology deltas without traces when no trace is recorded

IntegratedDistressLifeStatePolicy.deltas_without_traces runs the three stages'
expressions in one pass without the per-agent traces and dataclass copies, and
the runner uses it when the trace level is off. The stress feedback formula is
shared with explain_update. The deltas are bit for bit those of explain_update.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Take the saved checkpoint when forking at a saved minute

A fork at a saved minute restored the source from its Checkpoint and then
captured and restored it again for the child. When the source is the saved
Checkpoint restored and not advanced, with the same runtime state, the child
now takes that Checkpoint and the source's world.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read a forked branch's history through its parent instead of copying it

A fork recorded the child's rows by copying the parent's index rows, about
3.5 GB for a seven-day Run, so a second fork exceeded the store's capacity.
The index (version 2) now records each child's parent and fork minute; reads
take the branch's own rows and its ancestors' rows before the fork minute, and
the child stores only rows from the fork minute on that its ancestors lack.
Conversation turns stay with their branch; a rebuilt branch reads no ancestor.

message:
Index a long computation's saves in another process

A computation with at least eight saves sends each save's new records to one
indexing process (storage/index_writer.py), which ingests them in order while
the computation goes on. Only what ingest reads is sent; a send that does not
start at the index's offsets is refused. The computation waits when the index
is two saves behind and, at its end, until every save is indexed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Remove a new child's pointer when its first save fails to index

A fork saves the child's pointer and then indexes it. When indexing failed,
the pointer named a branch the index lacked, and a retry under the same ID was
refused. TimelineStore.fork now removes the pointer (and any status) of the
new child before raising.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Build a save's restore check on the documents and extend the last check's log

The world a capture's restore check builds is only compared and discarded. It
is now built on the captured documents instead of two copies of them, and its
EventLog is the previous check's log with the new records appended, instead of
indexing every record again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
